events.reason: Parkinson disease and restless legs follow-up

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Re: Paula Wisniewski, DOB 03/09/1979. Seen 03/21/2023.

Parkinson disease: remains well controlled on carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 three times daily. No motor fluctuations, dyskinesia, falls or hallucinations.

Restless legs: improved somewhat with steady sleep habits and less evening alcohol, still present several nights a week. Ferritin from your office last year remained low despite oral iron. If it stays low, IV iron would be a reasonable next step and is likely to help her legs more than anything I could add.

Exam on medication: normal mental status and speech; no tremor; tone and bulk normal; finger and foot taps without decrement; reflexes symmetric; gait and turning normal.

Plan: no medication changes. Prescription renewed. Return in 12 months.
Outside neurology

documents.title: Allergy season
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Pollen is brutal this year, eyes and nose. I'm taking loratadine every day. Can I add something? Nose is already bleeding easier from blowing it so much.

documents.title: RE: Allergy season
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Daily loratadine through the season is fine. Rinsing with saline (gentle, not forceful) helps clear pollen and is kind to the nose. I'd hold off on steroid sprays for now since they can dry the septum and make the bleeding worse with HHT. Keep the saline gel going at night. If you're still miserable in two weeks, come in.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
44F annual. Says she's 'fine, tired, same as ever.' RLS a few nights a week. Nosebleeds weekly. Periods heavy. Son is a junior now, driving, which she finds more stressful than anything medical.

Neuro letter (3/23) reviewed - stable, suggests IV iron if ferritin stays low.

Meds: carbidopa-levodopa 25-100 TID; ferrous sulfate 325 daily; loratadine prn.
Allergies: NKDA; shellfish; tree pollen/dust mites.
PHQ-2 0.

Exam: NAD, pale conjunctivae. Lip/tongue telangiectasias. Thyroid nl. RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P:
- IDA: CBC/ferritin today. She'd rather keep oral iron for now; we'll revisit IV iron if the numbers don't move.
- RLS/insomnia, HHT, PD: stable.
- HM: mammogram ordered. Flu + updated COVID 10/3. Pap due - she'd like to do it at a separate visit, front desk to schedule. Colon cancer screening at 45 next year.
RTC 1 yr / prn.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hemoglobin 9.9, a little lower than last year, and iron stores remain low. Chemistries normal. Please keep the iron going daily. If you notice more breathlessness, or the nosebleeds or periods get heavier, let me know sooner and we'll set up IV iron.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu L deltoid, updated COVID R deltoid, IM. No contraindications. VIS given. Observed, left without issue.

reports.text: Bilateral digital mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with prior studies back to 2019. Heterogeneously dense. No suspicious mass, calcification or architectural distortion.

orders.reason: Solid-food dysphagia, glossitis, iron deficiency anemia refractory to oral iron; due for colorectal screening at 45

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
44F. Over the past year solid food has started to feel like it sticks on the way down - bread, chicken substitute, rice if dry. Liquids fine. Slowly worse. She's been cutting food smaller. Tongue sore lately, especially with anything spicy. More tired than her usual tired. No heartburn, no chest pain, no weight loss (weight stable on our scale), appetite fine. No melena. Periods heavy, nosebleeds weekly.

Meds: carbidopa-levodopa 25-100 TID, ferrous sulfate 325 daily, loratadine prn.

Exam: pale. Tongue tip telangiectasias as before, oropharynx otherwise normal. Neck no mass, no thyroid enlargement, no nodes. Nails thin and brittle. RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT.

A/P:
1. Solid-food dysphagia + sore tongue in long-standing iron deficiency. Needs GI and an EGD. Referral placed; she turns 45 next month so GI can also take care of colon screening, and a lower look is reasonable anyway with chronic IDA.
2. IDA, worse despite years of oral iron. CBC/iron/B12 today. Asked GI to weigh in on IV iron.
3. Menorrhagia - overdue for a proper look. Will raise GYN once GI is arranged.
Return after GI.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Paula, your hemoglobin is down to 9.1 and your iron stores are about as low as they go, which can by itself cause a sore tongue and even swallowing trouble. B12 is normal. GI has your referral marked as priority. Keep the iron going in the meantime.

orders.order: Upper endoscopy with small bowel biopsy and colonoscopy
orders.reason: Dysphagia, iron deficiency anemia; colorectal screening
Iron deficiency anemia refractory to oral iron

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Re: Paula Wisniewski, DOB 03/09/1979. Seen 03/12/2024.

Thank you for referring this 45-year-old woman with HHT (diagnosed by pulmonology in 2021) and Parkinson disease, who has also been seen by neurology.

HPI: about a year of difficulty swallowing solid food, gradually getting worse; liquids pass normally. Fatigue comes and goes. Recently her tongue has become sore with spicy food. She denies chest pain, heartburn or regurgitation, weight loss and any change in appetite.

Diet: vegetarian, mostly vegetables and grains; she does not eat red meat.
Medications: carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 three times daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily with vitamin C, loratadine as needed.
Allergies: no drug allergies; shellfish.

Vitals: T 36.7 C, BP 116/72, pulse 84, RR 16, BMI 22.6.
Exam: pale. Nails dry and brittle with spooning (koilonychia). Cardiac exam normal. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Neurologic exam grossly normal.

Impression: progressive solid-food dysphagia and a sore tongue in a woman with severe, long-standing iron deficiency. The combination with koilonychia points to iron deficiency itself as the cause, though structural causes need to be excluded. Her iron losses are menstrual and nasal; a GI source and malabsorption (celiac) should be ruled out given the failure of oral iron.

Plan:
1. Upper endoscopy with small bowel (duodenal) biopsies, and colonoscopy in the same session, which also serves as her first colorectal cancer screening.
2. Tissue transglutaminase IgA sent today (negative).
3. IV iron: ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg IV, two doses one week apart, arranged at the infusion center.
4. Recommend gynecology evaluation for her heavy menses.

Gastroenterology

events.reason: Upper endoscopy with small bowel biopsy and colonoscopy

reports.text: Specimen: duodenum, biopsies (4 fragments). Microscopic: small intestinal mucosa with normal villous architecture, villus-to-crypt ratio preserved. Intraepithelial lymphocytes not increased. No inflammation, granulomas, organisms or dysplasia.
reports.conclusion: Duodenal mucosa within normal limits. No histologic evidence of celiac disease.

documents.title: Endoscopy and Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Procedures: esophagogastroduodenoscopy with duodenal biopsies; colonoscopy.
Indications: solid-food dysphagia, sore tongue, iron deficiency anemia; colorectal cancer screening.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. ASA II.

EGD: The scope passed easily into the esophagus under direct vision. Esophageal mucosa normal throughout, with no web, ring, stricture, mass or esophagitis. Z-line regular at 38 cm. Stomach normal on forward and retroflexed views. Duodenal bulb and second portion normal; four biopsies taken from the second portion and bulb for celiac evaluation.

Colonoscopy: Digital rectal exam normal. The colonoscope was advanced to the cecum, identified by the appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve. Boston bowel preparation score 8. Withdrawal time 9 minutes. The entire colon appeared normal. No polyps. No angiodysplasia. Retroflexion in the rectum normal.

Impression: normal EGD and colonoscopy. Duodenal biopsies pending.
Recommendations: proceed with IV iron as scheduled. Follow-up of pathology by letter. Next screening colonoscopy in 10 years.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: Gastroenterology Pathology Letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body: Dear colleague, the duodenal biopsies from Ms. Wisniewski's endoscopy on 4/4 are normal, with no evidence of celiac disease. Together with a normal endoscopy and colonoscopy, this supports iron deficiency from her menstrual and nasal losses with inadequate oral replacement. Her dysphagia and sore tongue should improve as her iron is repleted; I would like to hear if they do not. She is scheduled for ferric carboxymaltose on 4/11 and 4/18. Gastroenterology

medications.sig: 750 mg IV, two doses one week apart (4/11 and 4/18/2024)

documents.title: Infusion Center Treatment Record
documents.author: infusion nursing
documents.body:
Patient: Paula Wisniewski, DOB 03/09/1979. Ordering: Gastroenterology.

04/11/2024: ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg in 250 mL NS IV over 20 minutes. Pre-vitals stable. No reaction. Observed 30 minutes.
04/18/2024: ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg IV, same. Tolerated well. Patient reports a mild headache the evening after the first dose, resolved.

Course complete (1,500 mg total). Recommend CBC and ferritin no sooner than 4 weeks after the final dose. Copy to PCP.

documents.title: Voice
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I need an appointment, not urgent but soon. My voice has been going for about a month. It started sounding strained and now most of the time I can only whisper. No cold, no sore throat. I am teaching with a microphone and writing on the board. Also I'm not sleeping. Things are not good at home. Can I see you next week?

documents.title: RE: Voice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Paula, you're booked Tuesday 5/14 at 3:40 with your physician. If anything gets worse before then, or you have any trouble breathing or swallowing, please call.

reports.text: Transabdominal and transvaginal imaging. Uterus anteverted, 8.1 x 4.6 x 5.0 cm, homogeneous myometrium without fibroid. Endometrium 6 mm, uniform. Both ovaries normal in size with physiologic follicles. No adnexal mass. No free fluid.
Satisfactory for evaluation, transformation zone present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Re: Paula Wisniewski, DOB 03/09/1979. Seen 05/07/2024, referred at GI's suggestion.

45 G1P1. Regular monthly cycles with heavy flow, worst the first two days. Has been this way most of her adult life. Long-standing iron deficiency, recently given IV iron. HHT and Parkinson disease noted. She spoke in a whisper throughout; she says this is new over the past month and she is seeing you about it.

Exam: normal external genitalia, vagina and cervix. Uterus normal size, mobile, nontender. No adnexal masses.
Pelvic ultrasound today normal: no fibroids or polyps, endometrium 6 mm. Pap with HPV done today: negative.

Assessment: heavy menstrual bleeding with regular cycles and a structurally normal uterus.
Plan: we discussed options and she chose a levonorgestrel 52 mg IUD, scheduled for 5/21. Expect irregular spotting for a few months, then much lighter periods.

Gynecology

events.reason: Loss of voice, low mood, poor sleep

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: Voice loss after family conflict, low mood, insomnia

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
45F. Whispering throughout the visit, writes a few things down when she needs to.

About 6 weeks ago (early April) she had a terrible argument with her son, 17, and said something to him she regrets more than anything. Two days later he left to live with his father in another state. He isn't answering her texts. Within a day or two of the argument her voice sounded strained, and over the following weeks it faded to a whisper most of the time. No sore throat, no cough, no cold, no reflux. Swallowing is actually better since the IV iron.

Sad most days, lots of guilt, keeps replaying the argument. Hard to fall asleep and wakes repeatedly. Still enjoys her garden and her students. Eating normally. No thoughts of harming herself, now or ever; husband supportive. Teaching with a mic, avoiding phone calls.

PHQ-9 11.

Exam: whispers, but coughs with a normal strong cough. Oropharynx normal. Neck supple, no nodes or mass, thyroid normal. Lungs clear. RRR. Cranial nerves grossly intact. Affect tearful when talking about her son.

A/P:
1. Loss of voice beginning right after a major emotional event, normal throat, strong cough - likely functional; low mood, guilt and insomnia alongside. Psychiatry referral today, she's open to it. Discussed crisis line and calling us if things worsen.
2. IDA - CBC/ferritin today, 4 weeks after IV iron. GYN IUD next week.
3. RLS/insomnia - worse with all of this.
F/u after psychiatry, sooner prn.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Some good news: the IV iron worked. Your hemoglobin is 11.8 and your iron stores are now normal for the first time since you've been with us. Psychiatry has your referral; their intake coordinator will call. Thinking of you.

medications.sig: Levonorgestrel 52 mg IUD inserted 5/21/2024 by gynecology

documents.title: IUD Insertion
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body: Procedure: levonorgestrel 52 mg IUD insertion. Consent signed. Urine hCG negative. Bimanual: uterus anteverted, normal size. Speculum placed, cervix cleansed, tenaculum applied. Uterus sounded to 7.5 cm. IUD placed at fundus without difficulty, strings trimmed to 3 cm. Minimal bleeding. Tolerated well. Instructed to check strings, expect spotting. Follow-up in 6 weeks for string check if desired. Copy to PCP.

conditions.label: Functional neurological disorder with speech symptoms (functional aphonia)

documents.title: Psychiatry Consultation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Re: Paula Wisniewski, DOB 03/09/1979. Outpatient psychiatric evaluation 07/01/2024. Referred by her primary care physician.

Identifying data: 45-year-old married high school math teacher with HHT, Parkinson disease, iron deficiency anemia and restless legs, seen four months after GI evaluated her for dysphagia and a sore tongue related to iron deficiency.

Chief concern: increasing trouble speaking over three months.

HPI: In early April she had a heated argument with her teenage son and told him she wished she had never raised him. He left two days later to stay with his father in another state, and they have had little contact since. Her voice became strained right after the argument and she has since lost the ability to project it; she whispers or writes notes. No sore throat, cough or recent respiratory illness. She describes a persistent sadness and intense guilt over what she said and keeps returning to the moment. Sleep is broken: it takes her a long time to fall asleep and she wakes often, sometimes replaying the argument. She finished the term at school but avoided the phone and stopped speaking up in staff meetings, and colleagues commented that she seemed withdrawn. She still enjoys her usual activities but has been socializing less because of her voice. No flashbacks, intrusive images or nightmares about the event. No hallucinations or delusions at any time. No meaningful change in weight or appetite. Since April she also describes near-constant worry that she finds hard to switch off, with muscle tension. No fever, neck lumps or swallowing problems now.

Psychiatric history: none prior. No previous treatment. Family: mother with generalized anxiety disorder and hypothyroidism.
Substances: wine occasionally; never smoked; no drugs.
Safety: denies suicidal or homicidal ideation; future oriented; supportive husband.

Mental status: well groomed, cooperative. Speech is a whisper with normal articulation and language; she can cough normally. Mood "guilty." Affect constricted, visibly anxious when the argument is discussed. Thought process linear; no psychotic content. Cognition grossly intact. Insight and judgment good.
Brief exam: oropharynx normal; cranial nerves intact.
GAD-7: 13.

Assessment:
1. Functional neurological disorder with speech symptoms (functional aphonia), onset after an acute interpersonal stressor, with a normal oropharynx, intact cranial nerves and a preserved cough.
2. Generalized anxiety disorder.
No PTSD, no psychotic features.

Plan:
- Explained the diagnosis as a real, reversible problem with how the voice is being controlled, not damage to the voice box.
- Referral to speech therapy for voice retraining.
- Weekly CBT-based psychotherapy here, focused on the guilt and worry, sleep and reconnecting with her son.
- No medication at this time; she prefers therapy first.
- Follow-up in about 3 months.

Thank you for this referral.
Outpatient psychiatry

documents.title: Speech Therapy Voice Evaluation
documents.author: speech therapy
documents.body:
Outpatient voice evaluation 07/09/2024. Dx from referring psychiatry: functional aphonia.

Presentation: whispered phonation in conversation since April. Throat clear and cough are voiced and strong.

Trial therapy: circumlaryngeal massage, then voiced cough to sustained 'mm-hmm', to vowels, to words. By the end of the session she produced clear voice in single words and short phrases, which surprised and moved her.

Plan: 4-6 sessions over the summer to stabilize voice in conversation and on the phone; home program given.

Addendum 07/23/2024: third session. Conversational voice normal in the clinic and on a phone call to her husband. Will continue one or two sessions after her trip if needed.

Speech-language pathology

documents.title: My voice
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just wanted to tell you, my voice is coming back! Speech therapy has been amazing. I'm still seeing the therapist at psychiatry every week. Thank you for sending me.

documents.title: RE: My voice
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That is wonderful news, Paula. Thank you for letting me know. See you at your physical in September.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
45F annual. Speaking in a normal voice - first time I've heard it since spring. Voice came back in July with speech therapy and has held, including in the classroom this month. Still in weekly therapy with psychiatry. Sleep still broken, RLS a couple of nights a week. Swallowing completely normal, tongue fine. Periods much lighter since the IUD, some spotting.

Meds: carbidopa-levodopa 25-100 TID; ferrous sulfate 325 daily; loratadine prn; LNG-IUD (5/2024).
Allergies: NKDA; shellfish; tree pollen/dust mites.
PHQ-9 5, GAD-7 8.

Exam: well, not pale today. Normal voice. Lip/tongue telangiectasias. Thyroid nl. RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Nails improving. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P:
- IDA: CBC, ferritin, CMP, TSH. Continue oral iron.
- Functional aphonia: resolved with SLP. GAD: in CBT with psychiatry, improving.
- HM: colonoscopy 4/2024 normal (10 yrs). Pap/HPV 5/2024 normal. Mammogram ordered. Flu/COVID 10/1.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your hemoglobin is 12.6 - normal! Iron stores normal, thyroid normal, chemistries normal. Keep up the daily iron.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Trivalent flu L deltoid and 2024-25 COVID R deltoid, IM. Screening negative, VIS given. Observed 15 minutes, fine.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Re: Paula Wisniewski, DOB 03/09/1979. Seen 10/08/2024.

Paula's voice is fully back and has stayed normal through the start of the teaching year, including phone calls. She finished speech therapy with a last session in late August, after a trip abroad. She continues weekly CBT; guilt and worry are less consuming. Sleep remains her main complaint: slow to fall asleep, waking several times. GAD-7 7 today. No medication; we will continue therapy and revisit sleep at the next visit.

Diagnoses: functional neurological disorder with speech symptoms, resolved symptomatically; generalized anxiety disorder, improving.
Follow-up in 4 months.
Outpatient psychiatry
